articleTitle: The Improving Efficiency of Electric Receivers on the Industrial Enterprises in Case of Short-term Power Outages
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article describes the two way to prevention short-term power outages first is the using increase field-forcing ratio of synchronous machine and second is the using batteries and supercapacitors of high power.

articleTitle: Towards the Character and Challenges of Partial Discharge Pattern Data Measured on Medium Voltage Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: To detect a fault behavior on medium voltage overhead lines is the key motivation of our research that produced several different metering devices, various long-time real deployments and many academic contributions and experiments. This paper aims to introduce the largest publicly shared dataset having more than 25000 different labeled signals. In the previous phase of our research, we were able to host an international data science based competition on a Kaggle platform while this data sharing tents to invite even more researchers and scientists. We expect that such a data share will open more possibilities into a deeper analysis and wider range of applications.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Stray Currents
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nowadays, the issue of stray currents is very actual, especially due to origin of electrochemical corrosion of storage devices. The biggest sources of stray currents are direct current traction systems such as railways and city lines using rails as a return conductor. In many cases, the return current does not flow back to traction converter substation by rails but uses other paths such as metallic devices stored under the ground (pipelines, metal-coat cables). This results in stray currents formation, which is the main cause of electrochemical corrosion. Electrochemical corrosion may cause serious damage of storage devices situated especially in proximity of direct current electrical traction systems. This paper deals with the issue of stray currents, describes the formation, spreading and the method of stray current measurement. The final part of this paper analyzes the results from real measurement of stray currents originating mostly from city tram lines. Measured data indicates a high activity of stray currents which can lead to damaging of metallic devices stored under the ground.

articleTitle: GaN power transistor switching performance in hard-switching and soft-switching modes
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the investigation of the switching performance of the GaN power transistors, while the focus is given on the comparisons of the performance within hard switching (HS) and soft switching, i.e. zero voltage switching commutation mode. For this purpose, specific testing device was utilized and adapted to switching requirements of selected transistor structure. Switching performance was identified in the way of power loss identification during the HS and ZVS commutation mode, whereby parametric evaluation in dependency on switching frequency and power load was done. The results show what is the amount of the power loss reduction when perspective transistor structure is used in combination with ZVS switching, even when very high frequency operation is considered.

articleTitle: Temperature Calculation of Overhead Power Line Conductors According to the CIGRE Technical Brochure 207
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: An overhead power line is a structure used in the electric power system to transmit an electrical energy. The performance of overhead power lines depends on their parameters. An important parameter of the power line in the power system is its thermal limit. This article deals with the temperature calculation of overhead power line ACSR conductors according to the methodology stated in CIGRE technical brochure 207. The calculated temperature is also verified by the measurement on a real power line. At the end of the article the maximum allowable current (ampacity) of ACSR conductors depending on climatic conditions is also calculated. Obtained results are compared with actual current limits (for summer and winter season) using by Slovak transmission system operators.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Model of Electric Vehicle Charging Demand to Distribution Network Impact Analyses
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Future distribution networks will be quite different to those, we know today. One of the main factors of impact regarding the distribution net, is the progress in the e-mobility sector. Most accurate modelling of such network is by using real data from the consumers, mainly gathering data from the e-mobiles. Availability of such data in our research regions (mostly where e-mobility is expected to be growing) is extremely low. This is due to complexity of gathering such data on large scale. There's a need for accurate predictions of users behaviour in long term. This article is dealing with modelling the customer's behaviour based on the international statistics and its implementation into the probabilistic model itself.

articleTitle: Sodium-Sulfur Batteries for Energy Storage Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper is focused on sodium-sulfur (NaS) batteries for energy storage applications, their position within state competitive energy storage technologies and on the modeling. At first, a brief review of state of the art technologies for energy storage applications is presented. Next, the focus is paid on sodium-sulfur batteries, including their technical layouts and evaluation. It is introduced the equivalent circuit model of the battery cell. At the end, there are presented the results from simulation model which was developed in Simulink to verify the proper function.

articleTitle: Capabilities and Visions of Broadband Power-Line in Smart Grids Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes Broadband Power-Line (BPL) technology in the smart grid area. Experimental measurements have been made that meet the communication requirements of smart grid applications. The measurements were performed according to standardised methodologies (RFC). The main goal was to verify suitability and potential for enhanced BPL channel utilization. This is an unused option for possible features which work independently of data collection from smart meters and power quality data acquisition.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Stator Winding Fault of Induction Motor Using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Three-phase induction motors are widely used in the industrial sector. Even if their construction is rather simple resulting in high reliability, some unexpected faults can occur during their operation. Among them, the stator winding faults belong to the most common failures. In this paper, the simulation has been carried out for stator coil-to-ground fault using COMSOL Multiphysics software. This failure causes highly unbalanced stator currents causing changes in rotor currents, motor inner torque, speed, etc. Some simulation results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Power Flow Analysis of Networks with Loads of Constant Current - Constant Power Factor Type
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Modelling loads as constant current loads is a common technique used for load flow analysis of distribution networks, however this technique is not able to represent the power factor of loads correctly. Typically, the angle of the current representing a load is set relative to the angle of slack bus voltage and not to the related nodal voltage, which is unknown prior the calculation. In networks with high R:x ratio and limited reactive power flow, the resulting error in power factor of individual loads is often relatively small and can be neglected. However, if the power factor of the loads has to be respected during calculation with high precision, modification of the standard calculation algorithms is necessary. This paper presents the modifications of standard load flow algorithms necessary to allow load flow analysis of networks with loads of constant current amplitude - constant power factor type. Algorithms presented in this paper were tested on a set of simple test networks with variable size to verify, how the presented modifications of standard implementations are affecting the convergence characteristics of the algorithms and the absolute accuracy of results. Experimental results have confirmed that all presented algorithms are able to provide accurate results and the impact on the speed of convergence is neglectable.

articleTitle: CPC-based reactive compensation at three-phase four-wire systems powered from asymmetric sinusoidal voltage source
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents the fundamentals of the reactance compensation of the unbalanced loads in three-phase four-wire systems supplied from a sinusoidal and asymmetrical voltage source. The whole balancing reactive compensation is based on the Currents' Physical Components (CPC) Theory. The reactance compensation in four-wire circuits requires the device to be included in a star structure to be able to compensate the reactive current and the current at the neutral conductor causing by the zero sequence asymmetry, and the device in a delta structure to allow compensation of the reactive current and current causing the asymmetry of the negative sequence.

articleTitle: Operation Cost Minimization of Domestic Microgrid under the Time of Use Pricing Using HOMER
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents operation cost minimization of a domestic grid-connected microgrid under a time of use pricing scheme. Modeling, simulation and optimization of the proposed hybrid microgrid system including traditional and renewable power sources, energy storage systems and loads are performed by HOMER software based on the total net present cost. Gonbadekavoos industrial park in north-eastern Iran is considered as a domestic grid-connected microgrid and input data such as load, solar radiation, wind speed and energy price profiles are adapted from Gonbadekavoos region. Different configurations of power sources along with energy price sensitivity analysis in three periods of low, intermediate and peak load periods are investigated. Obtained results illustrate impact of energy prices on the integration rate of energy generating units specifically renewable energy fraction in order to minimize the operating cost of microgrid.

articleTitle: E-mobility Impact on Supply in Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper evaluates the impact of chargers measured on the charger cable connection to the distribution grid. The paper describes characteristic points and methods of charging electric cars with AC and DC current. The impact assessment focuses on the flow of active and reactive power, the proportion of harmonics in the current and the impact on the voltage assymetry of the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Bi-directional Charger with a High Power Density for Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article focuses on the use of bi-directional chargers with high power density in smart grids. Furthermore, a selected atypical topology of bidirectional charger is described. This topology allows single-stage power transmission, which reduces switching losses and circuit complexity. The high power density determines the chargers to be used in electric vehicles, becoming important parts of smart grids. The assumed characteristics of the developed charger were practically tested on a functional prototype in two operation modes, i.e. charge and discharge modes.

articleTitle: Methods for Dynamic Stability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with dynamic stability assessment. It analyses application of two approaches for the transient (rotor angle) stability calculations. It compares results of the conventional time domain simulation tool with simplified direct methods.

articleTitle: Modeling of Luminous Flux Radiation to the Upper Hemisphere from Real Model of Town
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Article targets to show potential of software goniophotometer from point of view calculation of the luminous flux leads to the upper hemisphere from road lighting system. Basis for this article was real model of blocks of flats in Frydek-Mistek. Software goniophotometer was originally checked in terms of accuracy for calculation direct and reflected part of the luminous flux [1]. In next step was creating of basic model formed from several objects including buildings and road lighting system realized by five luminaires [2]. Software upgrade allows possibility of inserting calculation grid in sphere shape. These points represented normal illuminance in direction to the middle of sphere and behave like an imagine luxmeter sensors. Aim of implementation this net is update simulation program for calculation of the luminous flux radiated to the upper hemisphere from artificial lighting systems as basis for next astronomic calculation which are deeply focused on night sky luminance description [3]. Using this model will possible to do models of the artificial light radiation of whole towns contains not only road light systems, but other artificial light sources too. Principle is to include radiation characteristics of these big units to LDT file as a one luminaire with information about luminous flux and shape of luminous intensity distribution. This LDT file could be used for next calculations which will evaluate influence of big light sources to night sky luminance.

articleTitle: Influence of Voltage Dips on the Stability of Excitation of Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper studies a method of forming a mathematical model of a synchronous machine when exposed to voltage drops on the exciter. A local integral transform was used as a partial local Fourier transform for the transition from the continuous variables to the equations in finite differences of constant structure. After that, the reverse transition to the mathematical model of the constant structure in continuous variables.

articleTitle: Error Ratio Evaluation of Protection Core of Selected Older Distribution Current Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Current transformer (CT) is one of the vital devices for metering electrical parameters of distribution and transmission networks. Requirements and specification are described in technical standards for 60 years at least, but ageing and performance after some time of on-site operation have not been described in recent works well, especially in conditions similar to network and climate situation in the Czech Republic. Due to the intended aim of using output values for technical state estimation of network components in RCM strategy development, only protection cores measurement for error ratio evaluation was proposed. The results of two selected older oil-insulated current transformers (5P10 class) from distribution network are presented in the paper. The cores are measured according to the protection CT accuracy class, and also, matching measuring CT accuracy class for a general overview of CT accuracy only. The equipment used for measurement is described. The highest current recordings, ratio error evaluation and values are presented and depicted. Results applicability is discussed.

articleTitle: Decomposition of the load's current supplied from a sinusoidal and asymmetrical voltage source in accordance with the Currents' Physical Components (CPC) Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The subject of this article is to exhibit the possibility of describing three-phase circuits powered from an asymmetric sinusoidal voltage source. Determining the physical components of the current associated closely with specific physical phenomena makes it possible to distinguish the components of unbalanced from the active and reactive components. Each of these currents, excluding the active current, contributes to the power of unbalanced and reactive power, which should be minimized or completely removed from the circuit.

articleTitle: Small Hydro Power Plants Operating As Backup Source In Local Island
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article deals with possible small hydro power plant operation as a backup power source for of a small local grid in island mode. Mentioned grid covers area of a small community usually connected to main grid, but temporarily disconnected from the grid due to some technical malfunctions in the main grid. The island operation should not cover complete energy demand in considered community, but it should be capable to power main crucial facilities in the community (hospitals, public buildings, traffic lights, street lighting, water stations, broadcasting systems, etc.). Specific sequential connection or disconnection to or from the island must be defined in dependency on the local power sources capacity and duration of the island operation. The main task is to discuss and define features of the local island, conditions of operation and definition of proper power sources and their cooperation. Complete research deals with different kinds of small local or distributed power sources, but this article focuses mainly on hydro power plants from the category small hydro.

articleTitle: Hardware-in-the-loop Based Grid Compatibility Test for Power Electronics Interface
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The future power systems has a clear trend towards power electronic connected generation. In contrast to conventional power systems, dynamic characteristics of power electronic interface strongly depends on the implemented control. This leads to imperative changes in the test and validation method of power electronic interface. This paper presents a new test and validation method based on hardware-in-loop tests in order to adapt to the future power system. Through this new method, equipment manufacturers can speed up the development-testing-certification period of their product and obtain product certification. The grid operator can obtain a credible power electronic interface - grid system stability validation report with the model verified by the hardware-in-loop test.

articleTitle: Assessment of Energy Consumption in the Residential Building with a Heat Pump
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the accuracy of the calculation of the energy needed for the heating of residential buildings by heat pumps. The reference value is the consumption obtained from the actual time course of temperature and the heat loss calculated by solving the partial differential equations. This value is compared with the results obtained using average daily and monthly temperatures and using a static wall model without heat capacity. The calculations are performed for the Carnot heat pump and for the currently used WPL18 heat pump.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of LiFePO4 Battery Cell During Discharge with Constant Current
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article deals with the influence of constant current discharge of battery with focus on temperature analysis. For test purpose was selected 3.2V cell, which can be used for a wide range of applications as electric vehicles, photovoltaics and power storage. LiFePO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> cell with a capacity of 40Ah at discharge currents of 20A, 40A, 60A, 80A, 120A together with surface temperature analysis was selected. This thermal analysis also contains infrared pictures using a thermal camera at determined discharge currents.

articleTitle: Innovative Single Stage Isolated AC/DC Converter with Power Factor Correction
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The actual market of low and middle power battery charging power converters is mainly based on two-stage concepts combining PFC and DC/DC converter. The efficiency and power density of those systems are being improved by newer semiconductor technology with higher switching frequency and reduced appearance of switching losses. Adversely newer transistors represent a significant share of device cost and have a negative impact on total cost in case of a sole transistor exchange. This paper describes a perspective way how to minimize the dimension and optimize cost of isolated AC/DC converters by adapting to modern topologies.

articleTitle: Usability Assessment of Mathematical Models of the Bathtub Curve
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the options how to model of the Bathtub Curve and how to properly estimate failure intensity during operation time of a system. Firstly, the term “Bathtub Curve” is described. The main part is connected with the demonstration of three possible models how to correctly estimate the failure intensity during operation of a system. The main aim of this paper is to assess usefulness of all investigated models for the estimation of failure intensities.

articleTitle: Measurement of acoustic emission velocity in natural ester
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Paper presents velocity measurement results of acoustic emission (AE) signal propagating in natural ester. The velocity of AE wave is crucial especially in methods used for partial discharges (PD) localization and its value may influence the location, which is calculated based on arrival time. Experimental works were performed using piezoelectric transducer for AE signal generation (transmitter T) and hydrophone for AE detection (receiver R) immersed in an elongated tank filled with liquid dielectric at various distances d between T and R. The velocity was calculated based on time of arrival (ToA) of the AE signals propagating from T to R and distance d. The transmitted AE signal was modulated using a frequency range from 40 Hz to 400 Hz what enabled to determine the velocity values within the analyzed spectrum. Based on the gathered results it was stated that velocity of AE signal propagating in the considered oil decreases while increasing the distance between T and R. Furthermore the calculated values depend strongly from the frequency of the AE signal. For an exact calculation of location of PD occurring in this type of dielectric the appropriate value of velocity should be considered. It is also recommended that a correction factor related to distance between PD and AE sensor is taken into account.

articleTitle: Classification of OLTC defects based on AE signals measured by two different transducers
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The subject of the article is related to diagnosis of on-load tap-changer (OLTC) based on acoustic emission (AE) signals measured by two different transducers. The main advantage of the AE method is the possibility of its application during normal operation without having to turn off the device under investigation. Based on chosen parameters of the AE signal various defects of the OLTC may be recognized. A number of signals, gathered from laboratory tests, in which four types of typical OLTC defects were simulated, was applied for classification studies with the use of artificial intelligence methods. In particular seventeen different supervised learning algorithms were investigated, while their effectiveness was compared by using common measures. Based on the performed studies the best algorithm for each of the two applied transducers was determined. Results of the works in form of the chosen algorithm may be applied in an expert system for diagnosis of OLTC devices when using different AE measuring sensors.

articleTitle: Current Sensor with low inductance
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with design of current sensor introducing low inductance. The sensor is designed for a current up to 500 A and 120 kHz. Since the market offers several types of sensors suitable for the targeted application, they usually have problems with measured signal postprocessing. This paper describes the principle of operation and includes simulation results and measurement made on the laboratory prototype of the proposed sensor.

articleTitle: Correlation analysis of hotspot temperatures in power transformer – a case study
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a correlation analysis of hotspot (HS) temperatures in power transformers on the example of two representative units coming from over 1000-unit population of high voltage (HV) to medium voltage (MV) transformers. Analyzed population is characterized by relatively low load and high age. Measuring data form one year period with 1h steps are gathered for analysis by on-line temperature monitoring systems mounted in the transformers. Analyzed data consist of ambient temperature, winding HS temperatures and load. Conducted correlation analysis shows that regarding that fleet there is relatively low correlation between load and HS temperature, and HS temperature is mainly depended on the ambient temperature. Observed dependencies may be used for optimization of the present thermal prediction models of the HS temperature in terms of the application for some similar, low loaded transformer populations.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Study of Low-Voltage Ride Through of Wind Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator by means of STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The penetration of wind-generators and wind-parks in energetics sets different requirements to them. One of the main problems is insurance of low voltage ride through capability in short circuits. The article investigates the use of STATCOM for achieving this operation regime. Using a noniterative algorithm for calculation of electromechanical processes a mathematical model of wind permanent magnet synchronous generator is created.

articleTitle: Differential Protection for Converter Transformers in Three-Level Active- Front- End Large Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, simulation of large motor drives with three-level neutral point clamped converters and testing results of converter transformer differential protection are presented. The protected converter transformer is used for supply of active front end converters. The converter transformer itself must be protected by a relay being able to operate with highly distorted signals by higher harmonics. One should be aware that high content of harmonics (2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>) may cause problem with sensitivity and stabilization of protection. An appropriate simulation model of the converter transformer and three-level neutral point clamped converters with adequate control was developed in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Testing results of transformer differential protection operation for various disturbances are presented.

articleTitle: Application of Optimized Deterministic Methods in Long-term Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: power engineering computing; power grids; distribution networks; power supply quality; invertors; distributed power generation; static VAr compensators; photovoltaic power systems; smart power grids; power transformers.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Measurement Methods for Partial Discharges Generated on the Surface of Solid Dielectrics in Insulating Oil
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents the results of partial discharge measurements using the UHF method and the conventional electric method, which were carried out in a model system of electrodes for generation of surface discharges on a solid dielectric immersed in mineral oil. Two model systems were analyzed; in the first system, a teflon plate was used as a solid dielectric and in the second system a pressboard plate was used. The measurements were carried out in laboratory conditions for alternating voltage.

articleTitle: Measuring of Fault Distance Using the Fault Locator Function of Protection Relay
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article is focused on fault distance measuring with feeder protection relay REF630 from ABB and its function fault locator. This function provides impedance-based fault location. For measuring was used laboratory at Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science where is laboratory stand with inbuilt REF630 and fault module and where is also available module of transmission network. With those modules there were measured fault distance in case of phase-to-phase fault and phase-to-earth fault for various values of fault resistance. Parameters of typical 11 kV distribution network was set up in protection relay by ABB software PCM600. In case of phase-to-phase fault measured distance corresponded with parameters of model. However, in case of phase-to-earth fault measured fault distance was more than two times lower than our model. Measurement was repeated with parameters of zero sequence reactance equal to positive sequence rectance. Next results corresponded to our model parameters. All results confirmed assumption that higher fault resistance causes lower accuracy of calculated fault distance.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Light Sources Technologies of Vehicles Headlights Illuminating a Model Road
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents courses of measured values of vertical and horizontal illuminance on a sample section of a road. The model road was created at LIBROS safe driving polygon in Ostrava within the Comparative Measurement of Night Traffic Area, which was organized as part of the research task VI2VS/571 of BV III/I-VS programme entitled “Analysis of Road Traffic Participants Visibility so that it is possible to increase their safety in dusk and night”. Measurements were made for two model situations of road lighting: vehicle low beam headlights and a combination of road lighting and low beam headlights. Vehicles of the same type with low beam headlights with halogen, xenon and LED sources were used for the measurements.

articleTitle: Industrial Uniterruptible Power Supply Batteries Monitoring Augmentation by Infrared Camera
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are vital for different industries. Along with a rise in their complexity, the requirements for a UPS become more important. UPSs are meant to protect technologies from damage caused by various interruptions of an electric power supply. Advanced monitoring of UPS ensured by a battery management system (BMS) is able to prevent from more serious damage thanks to a mechanism of in-time and accurate battery-fault detection, which is based on voltage metering. This mechanism is widely used, but its use gets very expensive. This also poses an obstacle in the further applications of the battery systems. This paper gives an overview of Czech national standards aimed at batteries used in industrial UPSs. As the temperature is the second key indicator of a battery's health, the battery voltage being the first, our research aims to develop a low-cost UPS monitoring system using infrared thermographic measurements. The research builds on an assumption that overheating of a battery implies a state of damage. The paper describes the design of an extended automatized metering platform.

articleTitle: Impact of E-mobility on Unbalance in Low Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: E-mobility is a fast-growing sector that influences many industries. In this paper, we deal with possible influence of e-mobility development on the existing low voltage distribution network. The paper contains results of load-flow calculation with charging of electric cars in household and their analysis from of view of voltage values and voltage unbalance in the low voltage distribution net.

articleTitle: Ground Potential Rise and Lightning Overvoltages in Control Systems of Large Power-Plants under High Soil Resistivity
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Power-plants are sometimes built on massive bedrock with high soil resistivity thereby often resulting in less favorable grounding conditions. While grounding for applications with power system frequency can be achieved with large electrode areas, lightning strokes usually affect smaller areas with heavier impact. As a consequence a grounding system suitable for power system frequency is not necessarily capable of handling transient phenomena sufficiently well. A critical case is the ground potential rise when a large lightning surge propagates through the grounding system. The potential differences in different parts of grounding system may damage the connected wiring and equipment, depending on how grounding connections are made. New installations can be equipped with proper equipment but existing plants, especially those subject to detailed approval processes such as nuclear power-plants, often can't be modified easily. This paper evaluates the impact of lightning on a grounding system with different lightning surge propagation properties and finally presents a variety of solutions how to properly improve the transient protection for control equipment from a system point of view.

articleTitle: Arc Flash Risk Assessment - Overview of scope and different approaches in the US and in the EU
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper gives the extensive overview about the Arc Flash Risk Assessment (AFRA) procedures and methodologies used in US and in EU environment. For both regions, the overview of related standards and guides is given. The main part of this paper describes the complete AFRA scope including arc flash risk identification, risk assessment (calculation) and risk control (mitigation). The AFRA flow chart is introduced to graphically present entire AFRA lifecycle with three possible approaches for AFRA execution (at present).

articleTitle: Single-Wire Electric Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes experimental setup for efficiency measurement of electrical energy transmission via single-wire resonance line.

articleTitle: Evaluation system for power loss identification of perspective wide bandgap semiconductor transistors
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a system for measuring switching and conductivity losses for different types of transistors. The measurement system is composed of hardware and software that evaluates the total transistor losses from instantaneous values. The hardware part consists of a test board that includes a power supply, transistor driver, measurement points, transistor, freewheel diode and oscilloscope. The software part (GUI) is done in Matlab, which displays the measured voltage and current waveforms and the calculated transistor losses. The result of the article is the measured loss values at different switching frequencies and power.

articleTitle: Influence of the Angle Between Two Power Systems on Electromagnetic Fields of Overhead Double Circuit Power Line
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The issue of electromagnetic fields of overhead power lines is still nowadays widely discussed. There are two basic topics in this research field. The first one is the exposure to the fields and their influence on human health. Due to this plausible health risk many counties have established exposure limits for the public and workers. The second topic is technological. With new technologies and the era of digitalization and modern electronics there are new plausibilities how to use the complex information that electromagnetic field can provide us with. Electromagnetic field can give us information about voltage and current events in the power system. It is also important to quantify the fields and their interference with the surrounding infrastructure, like pipe lines, telecommunication lines ect. Both of this main fields relay on precise measurement or on exact calculation. The article deals with the effect of the difference in the angle of the two power system of the double circuit overhead power line on the value of intensity of electric field and magnetic flux density. It has been shown that the widely used simplification that calculates the field only as a result of parallel operation of two power systems on double circuit power line can be misleading in specific situations.

articleTitle: Influence of Partial Anisotropy on the Nominal Values Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article deals with the influence of the partial anisotropy of electrotechnical sheets metal for electrical rotating machine. Specifically, the article is investigated by influence, some nominal values. The outcome of which can be influenced by both the material and the conditions of the machine measurement. Using the Ansys Maxwell 2D simulation software, we attempted to describe behavior in different states, and we also propose a solution to this problem.

Author Keywords: deformation of the rotating magnetic field

articleTitle: Reducing the Impact of Transient Phenomena of Arc Furnace on Power Network Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of the transient phenomena caused by the operation of the electric arc furnace in the 22 kV network, describes the causes of their origin and proposes the possibilities of their reduction with regard to the fulfillment of the quality of electric energy. In particular, it focuses on assessing the short-term flicker rate and the use of the STATCOM device to reduce it. The analysis and subsequent reducing of transient phenomena impact was realized by simulations using the Matlab / Simscape Power Systems tool. The obtained results were evaluated in accordance with the valid European standards and legislation of the Slovak Republic.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality as a Crucial Element in Modern Electric Distribution Company
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The predominant goal of this article is to touch upon the usefulness of the so-called Augmented Reality (AR) technology with regard to its utilization in companies distributing electric power. AR is understood to be a real-time combination of real world imagery, typically in the form of images recorded by a camera, with digitally generated one. Additional elements have to be added to the camera-captured image in real time and the whole experience should be interactive in nature, as well as allow the user to move freely. After analyzing the current applications of the discussed technology, the authors propose its utilization within the scope of companies operating in the electric power-related branch of industry, with the major focus being put on enterprises specializing in electric power distribution, both in terms of network infrastructure management and organization of training sessions pertaining to key procedures and machine handling.

articleTitle: Behaviour of Fire Resistant Cable Insulation with Different Flame Barriers During Water Immersion
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Globally, emphasis is placed on increased security in the field of human health protection during the fire. That is, why fire resistant, flame retardant and halogen-free cables are more used in public buildings. Their using can improve fire safety and fire rescue capability. Although, the fire performance is a priority for these cables, we cannot neglect the others important properties of core insulation. Changes of electro physical properties may be related with modifications of insulation in order to limit smoke, fumes and halogen or improve their fire resistance and maintain circuit integrity of vital emergency services (e.g. fire alarm). New insulation materials and cable constructions should be tested for different operating environment and emergency situations. The intention of our experiment was to simulate unexpected events during operation such as flooding of cable systems and water ingress through the open ends of the cables or damaging of the sheath. The paper presents the results of laboratory tests of fire resistant cable insulated cores with different types of flame barrier in case of long-term contact with water.

articleTitle: Infrared Thermography and Computer Simulation in Research of PEM Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The method of infrared thermography was used in this paper to identify over-heated areas inside module of hydrogen fuel cells. This module fitted with polymer proton exchange membranes, is a part of a laboratory off-grid system that serves to storage of electricity gained from photovoitaic panels. Hydrogen is not an energy source but a storage medium and an energy carrier. Hydrogen module operation with insufficient cooling can lead to its overheating and destruction. The cause of this undesirable state is detected here by the help of computer simulation using suitable numerical model. An appropriate solution to this problem is proposed to allowed a more efficient and safe operation of this module of hydrogen fuel cells.

articleTitle: Implementation of Small Hydro Power Plants in Water Facilities
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the issue of the location of small hydro power plants in the water supply systems. Here are the possible positions of location the SHPPs in the water supply system. An important part of the water supply system problems are the resulting losses due to faults in the water lines, which are also caused by excessive pressure in the water supply system. To help with selecting a turbine for SHPP, an application was created. The application results are compared to the real ones.

articleTitle: The Energy Efficient Solution for Intelligent Lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The aim of this article is to introduce the intelligent lighting control system. The created control system is able to diagnose current conditions and control the lighting system operatively to achieve the required lighting standard at minimal energy costs. The developed system will thus further reduce the energy consumption of the buildings in which it will be applied. The system was created in cooperation with Südluft Systemtechnik and will serve primarily for lighting control of commercial kitchens.

articleTitle: The Effect of Dimming and non-Dimming LED Lights on the Quality of the Electrical Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the power supply of electric lights, focuses attention on the quality of the power source, which is directly related to the influence on the public electricity grid. Modern LED lights, which can be fabricated in different variants, are used in households and industry mainly for their economic operation. The reliability of these luminaires is many times longer than recently used neon tubes or lamps with tungsten filament. The paper compares the measured data from several variants of the LED lights dedicated to different applications for household or for industry. Samples of lights, which were compared, are lights for household, industry, and street lighting. Important quality factors are PF THD parameters with gradual dimming that is controlled by an external module or directly integrated in the luminaire case. These parameters are directly related to the impact on the public electricity grid. Measured values were recorded at 100%, 70% and 50% dimming.

articleTitle: An Approach to the Determination of the Harmonic Content of a Waveform by Analysis of its DC Component
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This experimental work is part of a larger project investigating the possibility of using a programmable controller (PLC) for condition monitoring of generators. Analysis of a generator's output current signature can yield information regarding its status. This paper proposes an approach based on the DC component of the generator's output voltage to determine whether it is sinusoidal or complex and to generate a binary signal to flag which condition applies. An Arduino microcontroller is used to make that determination and to generate a PLC compatible signal to flag the results. A series of experiments was carried out in order to test the capability of the proposed system over a range of harmonics. While this work is at an early stage, the results to date show promise and further work is proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of High Frequency Electromagnetic Field Penetration Through Building Material - Concrete Wall
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic shielding has been enjoying greater attention recently. On one side, it is due to the electromagnetic compatibility of electric and electronic devices. On the other, it is because of the electromagnetic effect on living organisms, a human being included. We are constantly exposed to the electromagnetic field which is why it is important to raise this issue. The proposed contribution presents the results of research into the shielding of a construction object concrete towards the electromagnetic field. Shielding is defined as shielding effectiveness. Shielding effectiveness is defined by a product of reflection and absorption of the electromagnetic field. The experiment in this contribution concentrates on measurement of shielding effectiveness and reflection of the electromagnetic field. Measured object was concrete wall 120 mm thickness composed of cement and water. Based on these observables it is possible to calculate the electromagnetic absorption which is difficult to measure.

articleTitle: The Control Process of an On-off Controller
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Regulation process of the two-position controller is defined by dynamic properties of the controlled system and by the control algorithm. This paper is focused on control of stable, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>order, continuous systems with overdamped step response. There are 2 main types of control algorithms of the on-off controller: comparative mode and fixed frequency mode. Both algorithms share a few differences, such as regulation time, precision and quality of control process. But the main difference is control logic. In the comparative mode, the controller output is switched based on the comparison of desired state and the actual state of a system. On the other hand, the control algorithm of fixed frequency mode is given by functionality between the input signal and the controlled variable. In addition to basic control algorithms, a new type of control was tested: hybrid mode. This mode combines advantages of comparative mode and fixed frequency mode, to improve dynamics of the regulation process of the two-position controller.

articleTitle: Reliability of the photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the reliability of the PV system's connection to the distribution network. The first part defines the conditions for the PV system's connection to the distribution network, while the second part defines the factors influencing the reliability of the PV system's operation and connection to the distribution network. The paper contains production data describing the failure and subsequent analysis of the failure of central inverters of the PV system. In the conclusion there are recommendations for the use of methods to analyse faults and to determine system reliability.

articleTitle: Combination of Biogas Station and Photovoltaic Power Plant Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article deals with the possibilities of cooperation of selected renewable energy sources in the distribution grid. This is a combination of the operation, or cooperation of, a biogas station with a photovoltaic power plant. The aim of the article is to outline several basic possibilities of cooperation of the above mentioned sources, including the introduction of technical aspects. To conclude, it proposes further solutions to the above problem, including their strengths and weaknesses.

articleTitle: Analytical Model for the Electrodynamical Forces inside Electrical Contacts of Commutation Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to present a new analytical model for the contact area of all switching devices, at all voltage and current levels. It was proposed in order to recalculate all the computational formulas related to the electrodynamical forces which inevitably appear in a mostly symmetric contact, with a different shape, other than a sharpen or pointed one. When applying this model, the very simplifying hypothesis of the constant current density on equipotential stiction surfaces for the crossing current is completely abandoned. These new expressions could experimentally be verified by means of a simple device. By using this model, we can study the “attraction”, electrodynamical forces that may appear in an electrical contact belonging to any switching device used in electrical and power engineering technique. This research could improve both design and maintenance of new and existing switching equipment like contactors, low voltage switches, oil submersed switches or even SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> high voltage ones.

articleTitle: Selection of chosen model parameters for technical and economic analyzes of the power system
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents a technical and economic model used in development analyses of the Polish national power system (NPS). Selected problems and proposals for solutions allowing for the optimization of calculations for the formulated model will be presented. Practical aspects of analysis and application of results to NPS will be presented.

articleTitle: FEM Models of Rotor Failures in Comparison to Real Measurement of IM by External Stray Field
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the validation of the 2D FEM model of induction motor with rotor failures. Output results of FEM analysis are compared to the real laboratory measurement of asynchronous motor. External magnetic stray field is used like the basic diagnostic method of it. The main parameter to be analyzed is the induced voltage generated on the coil, which senses the external stray field in radial direction of motor axis. Fast Fourier Transformation is used to evaluate the individual components of the voltage spectrum according to common diagnostic procedures. 2D FEM model of asynchronous motor has the same parameters of real motor in laboratory including nominal output power, rpm, power factor, voltage and current. Irreversible machine failures are created with adjustment of rotor bar by drilling or in case of eccentricity by misaligned setting in bearings.

articleTitle: Analyses of Trolleybus Recuperation Energy Utilisation Losses Considering Different Efficiency Ratios of Traction Inverter and DC/DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper analyzes a case study on the efficiency of reuse of braking energy for electric public transport equipped with a mobile energy storage system depending on the efficiencies of the drive inverter and the DC/DC converter. Firstly, the simulations of the braking energy accumulation process were carried, followed by simulations of the process of reuse of previously stored energy. Losses in the accumulation process and losses during reuse were deducted from the full braking energy. Simulations of both new and used energy storage systems were carried to study also the effects of aging.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Assessment in the Proximity of High Voltage Power Station Equipment
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the proximity of high voltage overhead lines or high voltage power equipment located inside power stations, high values of the magnetic field induction (and/or electric field intensity) could appear sometimes, too. Safety measures, both for environment as well as for human operators are mandatory. The realistic assessment of the magnetic field induction nearby these facilities is one important stage before adopting new design features or limiting the human exposure. This paper presents some measurements of the magnetic field induction, taken by our team, mostly at the Fantanele 220 kV/110 kV/20 kV Power Station, located in the Central Region of Romania and owned by the National Power System Operator, TRANSELECTRICA S.A. This case study will be completed with some electrical field measurements, for a better perspective on the electromagnetic field parameters. Data is also used for the refurbishment of the existing power facilities.

articleTitle: Parameters for modelling of increase EV numbers use
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article is dealing with parameters which need to be considered for wider grow of using electric vehicles. Parameters are from broad ranges - technical, financial and even psychological. Humanity is facing unheralded changes in living condition. A huge using of fossil fuel-based technology enable us to grow in population, but it caused a significant imbalance in the Earth resources and unwise use of them for short prosperity.

articleTitle: Open Phase Fault Localization in a Medium Voltage Distribution Grid Using Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on an open phase type of fault in a medium voltage (MV) distribution grid. This phenomenon is described from the perspective of two mainly used configurations of connection of MV transformer windings. The analysis of how to detect the fault is drawn up from measurements in an MV as well as low voltage (LV) grid. Theoretical analysis is followed by a digital simulation for its verification and real measurements were also done in the grid. The use of smart meters is considered to be a reliable economical-technical approach in an open phase fault localization process.

articleTitle: Study of Low-Voltage Ride Through of Wind Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator by means of STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Within the conception of green energy spreading more and more the wind generated energy became a promising source of electricity. The connection of wind parks to the net however causes problems concerning the stability and the quality of electro energy. The work of power system is sensible to the disturbances in the net and it is necessary to provide the low voltage ride through of wind synchronous generator consists from permanent magnets by the help of system devices like STATCOM. Using a mathematical model it is investigated the behavior of the generator and compensator by different disturbances in the net. Using different approaches and algorithms their control is investigated.

articleTitle: Calculation of Losses in Transmission System in Dependence on Temperature and Transmitted Power
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Losses occur on all elements of the transmission system. While they cannot be eliminated, they can be minimized. Losses can be measured or calculated using transmission line parameters. The accuracy of the calculation depends on which loss causing influences are taken into account. Among the most important external loss causing influences is the effect of the ambient temperature. The paper compares results of calculation of technical losses based only on line parameters taking into account the ambient temperature in relation to a particular transmission system using prediction software. Further, it deals with technical losses caused by a configuration change of a selected part of a transmission system related to the operation of Dlouhé Stráně pumped storage hydro power plant.

articleTitle: Detection of Local Softening, Welding and Formation of Metallic Bridges between the Copper Contact Pair Using Temperature Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: A paper is focused on the analysis of local softening, welding and formation of metallic bridges between the copper contact pair using temperature rise measurement. The contact pair is one of the most important and, at the same time, most problematic parts of the current-carrying path of electrical switching apparatuses, because of its power losses. Amount of power losses is mostly affected by a contact force and by a type of used contact material. Inappropriate choice of these parameters could lead to the extreme heating of contact pair and whole device. A material of contact is affected by a high temperature. Phenomena called local softening and welding may occur due to the high temperature. Metallic bridges create a permanent connection between the contacts. This permanent connection decreases a contact resistance, but unfortunately it disables the function of the entire switching device - the ability to break the electric circuit. The paper shows one of the possible solutions to the problem with on-line detection of phenomena between contact pair using temperature rise measurement.

articleTitle: Influence of Changes of Material's BRDF on a Skylight Performance under Various Exterior Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article describes the results of the characteristics of a set of selected light pipes in different sky conditions. The first light source is the CIE Standard Overcast sky and the second is the partly cloudy sky with brighter circumsolar on the 21st of June. The light transmission efficiency of the light pipe with the ideal mirror-coated surface and a standard aluminum mirror is observed. Furthermore, differences in the use of the clear cupolas from the glass or from the PMMA are shown. The results show an unequable decrease in light transmission efficiency with increasing of skylight length.

articleTitle: Improving the Operating Parameters of the 300 kV AC Test System
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The High Voltage Test Laboratory in CVVOZEPowerLab is equipped with a Haefely Hipotronics HV Test Transformer HHT7300-300T5-760. This test system is used for withstand voltage, breakdown voltage tests and diagnostics of dielectrics - measurement of partial discharges and electronic bridge measurement up to 300 kV. Unfortunately, the system produces output voltage with high value of harmonic distortion, mainly in the condition of low output load. Higher harmonics in the output test voltage make it impossible to carry out accurate withstand tests and affects the measurement accuracy of the dissipation factor and the operation of the PD system. These problems were solved for last 5 years and currently are found several partial solutions. In this paper are described several basic concepts used to improve the operating parameters of the 300 kV AC source.

articleTitle: The Practical Correction of Wavelength Uncertainty of Array Spectroradiometers
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article has task to inform a reader about wavelength uncertainty of array spectroradiometers and propose corrections that can be performed on measured spectral data or moreover on photometric quantities that are already calculated from measured spectrum. Therefore, a several array spectroradiometers are tested on spectral accuracy and corrections coefficients are calculated for illuminance measurement for typical spectrums of fluorescent and LED light sources.

articleTitle: Optimized Use of the Steam Accumulator in the Combined Heat and Power Production
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents technical analysis of the usage of steam accumulator in the combined heat and power production and also in all general steam production. Created mathematical model is possible to use for evening on wanted slope of steam flow change.

articleTitle: Change of Loss Factor On the Surface of Transformer Paper Due to Thermal Degradation
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This publication deals with changes in the loss factor on the surface of the impregnated transformer paper in the event of thermal degradation. The theoretical part discusses the properties of insulating materials used in the chosen experiment and a description of the impedance spectroscopy method in the frequency domain. The practical part contains experimental description, used transformer paper samples impregnated with different types of transformer oil and analysis of measured results with dependencies of loss factor, depending on frequency.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Dielectric Parameters of PE and PVC Insulations
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on measuring the electrical properties of samples of insulated cables from several different types of polyethylene and polyvinyl chloride using an automatic electric bridge. The paper shows the change of dielectric properties at different insulation loads with subsequent comparison and evaluation.

articleTitle: Laboratory tests of the influence of the shape of electroadhesive pads on the value of the attraction force
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article contains a description of the phenomenon of electroadhesion, the mechanism of its working and formation, as well as application possibilities. The paper also presents the concept of a research system based on a plate (pad) used to generate electroadhesive force. Experimental studies of the influence of temperature, pressure and humidity on different components depending on the material, grammage and weight are described.

articleTitle: Parallel Winding of a Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the design of seven times parallel synchronous generator winding. The parallel winding is not commonly used for synchronous generators because it could be a possible source of difficulties, especially compensatory currents. The paper mentions the design, simulations, manufacturing and results of a measurement performed in a power plant.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of PVC leads
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper theoretical and experimental results are presented relating to the polarization which appears as a consequence of non-uniform temperature spacing in cable insulation. This temperature gradient has both a short term influence and a long term influence. In the brief time the gradient creates mainly a conduction inhomogenity. This means that the conductivity of insulation adjacent to the heated core is higher than conductivity of insulation at outer radius of the cable. After a long time operation the changes of conductivity became massive due to chemical reactions accelerated in the places with higher temperature. All these processes give rise to the interfacial polarization which is created in insulating material with non-zero gradient of conductivity or permittivity. In our work we try to identify the mentioned interfacial polarization in a specimen of commonly used PVC cable. It was found, that the polarization appears at frequencies of the order of a few mHz. Measurement in this scale requires a special apparatus as it is sensitive to any perturbation. Here we are dealing with the problem of separation of polarization part from the conduction part of dielectric data. Following our experiments the best way of date processing is the use of complex modulus formalism. Experiences with interfacial polarization induced by a temperature gradient will be utilized for monitoring the cable properties during a long-term ageing.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Stress on the Hybrid Fibre/Particle Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nanocomposites are the next generation of materials for various types of applications. Their advantageous properties are now often used in modern applications as coatings or as gas barriers. In the future, the combination of conventional materials and nanocomponents will be more visible than it is today. This is due to their enhancing effect on the base material. Today's experiments with nanocomponents also include commonly used high voltage materials, such as epoxy resin. In combination with nanocomponents, the positive effect on the electrical, mechanical and also chemical properties is observed. One of the important attributes is a life span of the material, which means the preservation of optimal parameters in time. Importance of investigation of life span is to predict the time in which is safe to use the material without damaging the machine or, in the worst scenario, hurt a person. This article presents an experiment where the electrical parameters of nanocomposite materials under thermal stress are investigated. Pure epoxy resin, epoxy resin with nanoparticles and epoxy resin with hybrid nanoparticle/nanofiber filler were exposed to a temperature of 220 °C for 1000 hours. The positive influence of nanocomponents on the life span is observed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Disturbance in Industrial LED Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic disturbance of individual LED luminaires and the requirements of technical standards to limit it are well known. This paper focuses on the analysis of electromagnetic disturbance of entire industrial LED lighting systems with a high number of luminaires and hence high power consumption. In such large industrial lighting systems, the effects of electromagnetic disturbance may be very different from the electromagnetic disturbance of individual luminaires.

articleTitle: Impact of Combustion of Alternative Fuel in Low Power Boiler Installation on the Environment and Technical Parameters of the Boiler
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Due to depleting fossil fuel resources, the search for their substitute is becoming more and more frequent. Alternative fuels may contribute significantly to solving this problem. However, combustion of such types of fuels in small boiler installations is not commonly applied in connection with difficulties during their thermal processing. In order to safely utilise the energy contained in alternative fuels, it is necessary to learn about their properties, the impact combusting them has on the operating parameters of the boiler installations and natural environment. The research was performed at a laboratory site using a low power boiler. Alternative fuel was subjected to energy analysis, and the reference applied were results of studies of coal combustion. The PBO alternative fuel is a mixture of sewerage sludge with oat, whereas the GFC fossil fuel is a gas-flame coal. Pollution emissions were examined as well as impact of the fuel on the boiler operating parameters. Combustion of the PBO fuel was be a stable process. The emission of CO, NO2 and SO2 exceeded values obtained for hard coal combustion. CO2 emission during combustion of alternative fuel was lower in comparison to the fossil fuel. Thermal power of the boiler decreased by ca. 30% during thermal processing of the PBO fuel in relation to the GFC fossil fuel.

articleTitle: Adsorption in an Exhaust Gases Aftertreatment - Computer-Aided Calculations
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: After any combusting process, there is an amount of exhaust gas that can provide unwanted air pollution, caused by its temperature, certain products concentration, and dust. To decrease the undesirable effect on the atmosphere, there are being installed some installations into the whole powerhouse system, that are dedicated to lowering the danger of causing the environmental impurity. One of the processes, that affects the concentration of the specific product in the exhaust gas, is adsorption. To help, accelerate and simplify the engineering calculations, there are available some computer programs, designed to do so.

articleTitle: Inspection of nuclear irradiated fuel
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article deals with the inspection of nuclear irradiated fuel assemblies of pressurized water reactors (PWR). Fuel inspections are important for economical and safe operation of nuclear power plant. Several inspection methods are currently being developed which have their technological limits. The article gives an overview and discusses possible extensions inspection possibilities and their extension.

articleTitle: Analysis of technical condition of lignite-fired power units as the way of reducing the operational risks
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper the assessment of operational reliability of power units installed in the world's greatest lignite-fired power plant, which is Bełchatów Power Plant with capacity reaching 5298 MW, was carried out. Conducted analysis was based on stored in computer data base records of operational events that took place in all of the 13 power units since the first power unit was commissioned to the end of 2017.

articleTitle: On Stabilization of Voltage in LV Distribution System Employing MV/LV OL TC Transformer with Control Based on Smart Metering
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with stabilization of voltage level in low-voltage (LV) grids penetrated by dynamic loads and distributed generation units employing OLTC transformers with supporting distributed voltage measurement system along grid. For correct and effective regulation/control of the LV transformers, it is important to respect real voltage magnitude profile along the grid, to set appropriate tap. Deployment of Smart Metering offers an opportunity to obtain required voltage data in all points of connection. In terms of communication, power line communication is typically employed, nevertheless some limitations in data availability (due to communication delay or even temporary loss) for the transformers real tine autonomous control are expected. Various scenarios tested by means of simulations are proposed and performance of voltage stabilization systems of progressive technology level are compared and discussed in terms of their effectiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Reversible Coupling Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with a new universal coupling converter, which has been realized in form of a laboratory sample at Department of Electronics, FEECS. The circumstances of demand of a new coupling solution are presented firstly, descriptions of new concept and its function follows. Finally, the results obtained from the realized model are stated.

articleTitle: CAN Bus Comunication using LabViewSystem
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the CAN bus communication between the infotainment elements and the drive component of the car using LabVIEW system. In the introduction, it is briefly described the communications bus used in automotive systems. These include buses CAN, LIN, MOST and Flexray. It is described their basic features, benefits and utilization. The main task is graphically program and builds a dashboard that will resemble a real dashboard from a Volkswagen Golf 5. Using the virtual dashboard built in LabVIEW, it is controlled the real dashboard.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of the Inverter with Advanced Features
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with an increasing share of renewable energy sources connected into low voltage grids, related problems and possible solutions. Trends are moving to utilization of so-called advanced inverters. Main contribution of the paper lies in creating the model of such inverter, what is further described together with its implementation using Matlab Simulink software and Simscape Electrical componets library. Validation of model results with measured one is also provided. An example of using the model in a simulation for assessing the increase in voltage when connecting a photovoltaic with a conventional inverter compared to connecting using an inverter with advanced functions is shown. Evaluation of model performance is also carried out.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Importance of HV Switches According to their Location and Analysis of Protection Fault Logs
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper describes the next part of the work deploying Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) on selected network elements, specifically on the HV switches of the selected distribution company area. The success of the RCM implementation requires appropriate selection of criteria describing the status and a significance of the element and, at the same time, appropriate setting of the assessment of the particular criterion and its weight. We deal in more detail with the analysis of one of the criteria of importance - Evaluation of importance criteria according to their location in the network, and evaluation of the protection fault logs, which are the basis for the evaluation of one of the criteria of the technical condition - Short-circuit history index.

articleTitle: Energy harvesting systems for anticorrosive protection device
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In anticorrosive protection of metal underground devices (especially pipelines) are frequently used electric devices such as cathodic protections or electrical drainages. They are often situated in the field, far away from an electric power network. For this reason, their power supply is complicated. Alternative power sources like solar cells, thermoelectric generators, or stray current energy harvesting are sometime used.
