In case of cathodic protection relatively high power is required - from tens to hundreds of watts, so only a power network or (in some cases) solar cell is applicable. In case of electrical drainage, only power below 1W is required, so powering from alternative power sources may be used. Authors of this paper developed electric regulated drainage with several possibilities of powering, external power source (power network), battery, or energy from current/voltage between railway rails and underground pipeline, where drainage is connected. In this paper an energy harvesting system is described, which acquires energy from current flowing through drainage in forward direction, or from voltage on drainage in a reverse direction. Also laboratory and field testing results are given here. Furthermore, at the beginning of the paper is a basic explanation of electrical drainage principle.

articleTitle: Occurance of Oscillations in Transmission System of Slovakia
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Oscillations seem to be always present in the interconnected transmission system of continental Europe. There are ways to damp them, most of which are used in Europe system, but despite the effort of transmission system operators, the operational experience proves that oscillations threatening the system stability can still arise. Examples of such are oscillations from December 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>, 2016. Therefore, it is vital to monitor the presence of oscillations in the system and actively control them. Transmission system operator of Slovakia has, available for this task, a wide area monitoring system, which can evaluate parameters of the oscillations and warn the operators. This paper deals with the options of the system and shows modes of present oscillations.

articleTitle: Computer based Study about the Load Regime of a 40 MVA 110/6 kV Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The power transformer is probably one of the most complex and most important equipment existing in the power transmission and distribution system. The evaluation of the technical condition, done with the double purpose of extending its life and reducing the risk of defect, is a complex and important activity, depending on the importance of the transformer in the system. Whether it's routine investigations or special investigations that appeal to the latest techniques and methods of measurement, in order to get a correct diagnosis, the measured data must be as accurately determined, correlated and evaluated on the basis of applicable technical regulations, the latest recommendations and information from the literature, and last but not least, the similar experience. This paper will show a case study for the variation of the load efficiency (the yield) as well as some economical aspects, based on real measurements and technical data.

articleTitle: Application of the Designed Model of the Blasted Electric Arc under Various Argon Flow Rate
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The designed mathematical model of the intensively blasted electric arc burning inside the arc heater anode channel is based on the energy and mass conservation laws and Ohm's law. With the aim of decreasing the computational burden and making the model easy to understand for students, simplifying presumptions are included. Validity of them could be impaired when the model is applied with experimental data obtained under very different operational conditions. Thus, verification of the model should be made with the data measured in a wide range of gas flow rate, input power, radius and length of the anode channel, etc. In this contribution, attention is focused on the influence of the working gas flow rate, which is crucial for cooling and stabilization of the arc. Axial distributions of the arc temperature, radius and potential drop are computed for two argon flow rates differing by 100 percent, with other operational conditions unchanged. The results are illustrated in figures and discussed.

articleTitle: Laboratory Model of a Small Hydropower Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Small hydropower plants are currently an interesting area of renewable energy sources. For the further use of renewable resources, it is necessary to look for methods for the use of watercourse resources that were unproductive by means of standard concepts. From this perspective, small hydropower plants, which are plants with an installed capacity of up to 10 MW, appear to be promising. From a management optimization point of view, it is important to use the potential of the SHPP in the most efficient way. A key area of this issue is the management of these power plants so that the power plant is productive for the longest time. The laboratory model consists of two asynchronous motors, the first one operating in a motor mode and the other in a generator mode. Both machines are controlled by modern semiconductor converters that can monitor a variety of important variables for the whole system's analysis of this model. At the same time, this SHPP model is equipped with an electronic flowmeter and several pressure gauges for sensing non-electric quantities. It is important to know the connection between the hydrodynamic, mechanical and electrical quantities for the management of the SHPP. The characteristics of the operating modes are listed here based on measurements and allow for basic conceptions of the behaviour of these SHPPs.

articleTitle: Photovoltaics Integrated in Skylights and Facades of Modern Shopping Malls
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Replacing standard glazing, wall and roof facing materials with building integrated photovoltaics offers both, electric energy production and art expression of building envelope - roofs, skylights and facades. Daylight coming from skylights and large-scaled glazed roofs allows better perception of architectural elements and details of modern shopping mall. Electric energy production is important extra profit of such solution. In this paper we discuss specific technical, architectural and electric energy aspects of buildings - shopping malls with building integrated photovoltaics in Central Europe conditions.

articleTitle: Modelling of Cogeneration Units
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the modeling of cogeneration units. This model is programmed in Microsoft Excel. The input parameters are different, according to the required calculation requirements. The program can design a cogeneration unit for the specified mode of operation. It can also count on the economic side of the cogeneration unit's operation, which may include revenue in individual years, operating costs, green bonuses, cash flow, return on investment and other economic requirements.

articleTitle: The Impact of a Low-voltage Smart Grid on the Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the impact of a low voltage smart grid on the distribution system. The last European directives 2014/94 / EU, 2009/28/EC and 2010/31 / EU, bring new problems to solve for distribution system operators. The existing networks of distribution systems are not prepared to fulfill these criterions. Paper shows results related with application of this new directives on existing distribution systems.

articleTitle: Improvement of transient stability using STATCOM combined with optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Further improvement of FACTS (Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System) control can help to increase the transient stability of a power system without adding extra grid inertia. Sophisticated optimization algorithms and modern Computer Algebra Systems provide new means of controller synthesis for power systems. The paper presents an approach of enhancement of transient stability using FACTS devices, particularly STATCOM (Static Synchronous Compensators), combined with optimization. Furthermore, chapter 3 describes different ways of defining the objective function. Different approaches are compared using the case study model that was implemented in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of Black Start Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Paper deals dynamic calculations. It presents two cases for real black start tests and shows their dynamic simulation.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting from Discontinuous Flow
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with harvesting energy of airflow created by vehicle passing by crash barrier and use this energy for light signalization. To analyse this airflow and to design shape of a wind flap that harnesses as much energy as possible we used two-way fluid-structure interaction in ANSYS software. This wind flap is mechanical extension of piezoelectric element (piezoelement). At first we searched for the best shape of wind flap that is selected in accordance with analyses results. Few of best shapes were experimentally tested to verify analyses. Next step was design of electronics that accumulates enough of electric energy to power light signalling device (in our case LED) for a short time.

articleTitle: Complex Electrical Characterization of a-Si/c-Si Solar Heterostructures with Conductive Antireflection Coatings
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents results of the development of silicon heterojunction solar cells with a front high band gap amorphous silicon carbide emitter. The attention is focused on the optimization of deposition conditions of sputtered ITO. For the comparison as an alternative also IZO transparent conduction oxides (TCO) were prepared and measured. ITO (IZO) are key layers to attain good antireflection and collection properties. It is shown that sputtering current affects both optical as well as electrical properties of prepared ITO. Complex electrical characterization of prepared solar heterostructures was performed by using DC and AC techniques. Measurements were performed under the dark and light conditions. The obtained results show the usefulness of complementary approach in order to assess the behavior of measured samples. The best efficiency of 9.66% is attained with ITO layer deposited at low sputtering current.

articleTitle: A Combination of VSG and Amended Fractional-Order Repetitive Control for Improving Power Quality of Grid-Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nowadays, in the modern power systems, due to increasing the application of renewable energy sources, power inverters are most commonly used electronic devices in the energy systems for ac/dc power conversion. Since the standard power inverters have extremely low inertia elements, the modern power systems meet insufficiency inertia to maintain the grid stability. In virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technique, virtual inertia is emulated in the power inverters by implementing swing equation and as a result, grid inertia is increased and grid stability will be satisfied. Although grid inertia issue is solved by VSG control, dealing with some power quality problems, such as grid current harmonic, which occurs in bad situations, has not been considered in this control theory. In this paper, a control approach based on a combination of VSG technique and amended fractional-order repetitive control (AFORC) is presented for grid-connected inverters to cope with the mentioned problem. The results of simulation studies proved that the proposed method besides fulfilling the main VSG objectives, such as transient frequency response enhancement and increasing total inertia of the power systems, it also can extremely diminish harmonic components of the current injected to the grid in the presence of distorted grid voltage and unbalanced nonlinear rectifier loads.

articleTitle: Flue Gas Heat Recovery in High Efficient Coal-fired Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the issue of waste heat recovery in high-efficiency power units. Structures of flue gas heat recovery systems (FGHRS) are presented starting from the system with heating of flue gases after their desulphurization. Systems using waste heat of flue gas to heat feed water in low-pressure and high-pressure regeneration are discussed. In addition, the results of simulation are presented in order to assess the potential for efficiency increase by using a heat recovery system in the 900 MW class lignite-fired power unit.

articleTitle: Open Source Platforms for Dynamic Stability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Paper deals with dynamic stability assessment. It demonstrates options for the transient (rotor angle) stability calculations and compares results of commercial simulation tool with open source software in point of view usability in practical applications.

articleTitle: Off-Grid System for Warning or Signalling Lighting of Dangerous Sections of Roads
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In long term, there is a decreasing trend of accident ratio on Czech roads. This is happening thanks to better car safety systems, more efficient emergency services and quality of roadways. We got the idea, based on own experience, to decrease this accident ratio even more. This objective led to the development of a few measures on how to increase road safety, especially on sections with an obstructed view. The result of our research is a system based on the off-grid platform that is meant to work anywhere in the Czech Republic. This off-grid system is modular, and its components are the solar controller, photovoltaic panel, Arduino, laser range-finder, LED strip and accumulation in the form of batteries. This paper describes the development path of this system and its function.

articleTitle: Verification of EMTP-ATP Model for Induced Voltage in Parallel Conductors
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic field, generated by conductors under load, plays an important role in electrical power engineering. Such a field can induce voltage on surrounding conductive structure. This effect is especially significant in a case, where there is a long parallel conductor next to the existing power line. Electromagnetically induced voltage in parallel structures can be investigated by software modelling. EMTP-ATP is a software, which is widely used for electromagnetic transient simulations. In this paper, EMTP-ATP model was used for verification of a simple physical model of two parallel conductors.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Possibility of Active Residual Oscillation Suppression Using an Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article deals with the issue of active damping of undesirable residual oscillations. The model of a planar physical pendulum with a prismatic joint was chosen as a suitable model example. The chosen model can be identified in practice as a crane arm with a movable carriage. At present, the most common solution for suppressing residual oscillations is to use signal shaping circuits. Their task is to ensure the acceleration and deceleration without producing undesirable oscillation. The article analyses the solution of residual oscillation suppression using an embedded system for cases where the unwanted oscillation of a load has already occurred. This system should ensure the measurement, evaluation and consequent targeted influencing of the main control loop. This is the introduction of an embedded system for active damping.

articleTitle: Lightning Overvoltages in Electrical Power System of a Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes lightning overvoltage spikes in an internal network of a large power plant. The cases considered are direct stroke to the phase conductor of the connected power transmission line and back flashover resulting from the lightning stroke to the transmission tower or shield wire. To investigate the transmitted overvoltages through transformers, high frequency models of the transformers are used. The voltage rise at the secondary side of each connected transformer at different voltage levels in the house load network of the power generation plant is analyzed. Protective measures are compared in order the study how to mitigate the transferred overvoltage at the different house load power system levels and to ensure that the impulse voltage is within the basic insulation level (BIL) of the connected equipment. Simulations using different combinations of protective surge arrestors and protective capacitors are done and recommendations on overvoltage protection are presented.

articleTitle: Motor Overcurrent Protection in the Function of a Differential Protection
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Larger asynchronous motors must be equipped with a differential protection providing protection against short circuits on the motor winding. A very interesting and unconventional solution is the use of the overcurrent protection in the function of the differential protection. By applying this solution we obtain a very precise and sensitive protection without distortion and not susceptible to interference. This will result in increased reliability of asynchronous motors protection.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Using Waste Heat from Computers
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article describes the possibility of using waste heat generated by computers performing blockchain computational operations. It shows technical design of the computing station, analyzes the possibilities of transporting waste heat to heating systems through heat exchangers. It also includes the practical design of the computational station used for the production of heat in the family house and the simplified possibility of remote control of the station throughout the Internet.

articleTitle: Assessment of Effectiveness of Distributed Generation Support for Voltage Regulation by Means of Power Control
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with assessment of effectiveness of small and micro scale inverter based distributed generation (DG) support for stabilization of voltage in low-voltage distribution system (DS) by means of its output active and reactive power control. Based on decisive parameters characterizing operation of DS under voltage level to output power control of the DGs, three independent evaluation factors are presented. Performance of the evaluating factors is in the paper tested by means of a simple radial LV network model with DGs distributed along the feeder, allowing modification of PQ(U) control strategy and of disponible power of the DGs parametrically. As a benefit from the performed extensive analysis, optimal PQ(U) control strategy is discussed and finally proposed.

articleTitle: Investigating the Suitability of Blockchain for Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The electrical grid evolved markedly over the past years and new Smart Grid phenomenon was born. Many new technological trends and concepts were introduced including also the blockchain. In the recent years, many theoretical ideas of using blockchain in Smart Grid were discussed, which resulted in new start-ups and test pilots deployed. This paper focuses on the investigation of peer-to-peer blockchain based energy trading suitability. We offer more broad discussion on the challenges and issues related with the selected application, which should help to understand the relations between application levels.

articleTitle: Physical Phenomena that Affect the Effectiveness of the Energy Transfer in Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The effectiveness of the energy delivery from its producers to customers is affected by a number of physical phenomena, but the nature of these phenomena is unclear and debated over a century. This debate has resulted in a number of power theories and a great variety of definitions of different power quantities. All of them are mathematically correct but differ as to the interpretation of the physical phenomena which accompany the energy transfer and affect the effectiveness of this transfer. These definitions and physical interpretations affect the method of the power factor improvement and unfortunately, they can cause a compensator malfunction. Presently, the most advanced power theory is based on the Currents' Physical Components (CPC) concept. Results of this theory are used in this paper for a discussion on physical phenomena which affect the effectiveness of the energy transfer in electrical systems.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Photovoltaic Power Plants Connectable Power Increasing in Low Voltage Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with calculations of maximum values of photovoltaic power, which can be connected into low voltage distribution grids regarding to currently valid legislation. A particular distribution grid, consisting of a radial feeder, is considered. The calculations are carried out for several variants that are expected to have a positive impact from connectable power increasing point of view. Variants involve utilization of autonomous inverters regulation functions or reinforcement of the distribution grid infrastructure as well as the combination of these options. All of the variants are subsequently compared and evaluated. For each of them, based on a theoretical analysis, a potential for increasing of connectable power in the considered distribution grid is quantified.

articleTitle: New User-Friendly Software Application to Simulate and Visualize The Distribution System Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new software application that simulates and visualizes the operation of the electrical distribution system (DS) and so helps understand various process occurring in the DS. The application runs on Windows operating systems and consists of five parts: DS modeling subsystem, DS parts' parameters settings subsystem, DS operation simulation scenario creation subsystem, DS operation simulation visualization subsystem, and mathematical core. This application is the result of an effort to connect two areas of engineering research that have not yet been well connected, particularly the power system simulation software development and the data visualization software development. This application features a graphical user interface that enables users to create a DS operation simulation easily and quickly, and to understand and easily read many values during DS simulation visualization. We aimed at user-friendliness and quick-adjustability of the application. The accomplishment of these goals was tested by a group of experienced university students in the course of one year. The students also participated in a survey. The application was created using the programming language Matlab.

articleTitle: Selected aspects of the electric energy supply security assessment - case study Poland
publicationTitle: 2019 20th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, analysis and assessment of Polish electric power infrastructure in area of generation in aspect of electric energy security is shown. This paper shows profile of generation sector in Poland and determines present and future situation in a range of its operation in frames of National Electric Power System in the context of security of electric energy supply. Moreover, threats of electric energy supply security in Poland are defined and catalogue of essential actions for assurance of electric energy supply security is proposed.
